A.name: The Missed-Call Leak
A.desc: Booking-process leak angle. Emergency wildlife caller is already panicking — your site loses them at the booking button before the phone even rings. $8K-$24K/mo anchor. Tease third issue. Dual-path close.

beats.title: Cost-Led Leak Open
beats.line: Hey, my name is {caller} with CritterClick. I audit wildlife removal websites all day. Yours has a leak that's costing about $8K to $24K a month in lost jobs. Who's the best person to talk to about that?
beats.followup: Got it — give me 30 seconds and I'll show you exactly where the leak is.
beats.note: COLD open, cost-led + gatekeeper-aware. Lead with the LEAK and the $ MONTHLY cost (reason to route), then ask 'who's the best person' — works whether you hit the gatekeeper (transfer) or owner ('that's me'). Calm Miner tonality, short breath-lines, slow the last line. CritterClick register: friendly authority, no fear-mongering, no kill-talk. Anchor = ~5-10 lost jobs/wk x $400-$600 = roughly $8K-$24K/mo.

beats.title: Emergency Caller, 3-Second Window
beats.line: Here's the deal — when a homeowner hears something in the attic at night, they Google, tap the first ad, and decide in about 3 seconds whether they're calling you or moving on. Wildlife removal is emergency-service buying — that caller will hire the first shop that makes it easy to reach them. When was the last time someone on your team pulled up your site on a phone and tried to call or book right from it?
beats.followup: Yeah — that's the most common answer. The booking button is just the first leak. The bigger ones come after.
beats.note: Plain English. Emergency-service mindset. Ends with a question they can't confidently answer.

beats.title: The Booking Button Costs You the Job
beats.line: Here's what's actually happening. The homeowner taps your ad, counts to three, and your phone number isn't front and center — so they back out and tap the next shop. The next shop picks up, gets the job — and gets paid for it. The ones who do find your number land on a booking process that asks them to fill out a form before they've even said what's in their attic. By the time they figure it out, they've already called two other shops. That's the $8K to $24K a month. Getting your phone number visible and making it easy to book — those are week-one quick wins. But there's a third issue on your site that costs more than both of those combined. I'd rather show you that one with your page open.
responses: How much would this cost to fix?
beats.followup: Fair — and that's exactly what the audit answers. Pricing comes after.
beats.note: Tease the third issue. Do NOT reveal it on the call. The reveal is the audit. Dollar-anchor the competitor steal.

beats.title: 100+ Wildlife Sites, Same 3 Leaks
beats.line: I've done this on over 100 wildlife removal sites — same 10-point checklist, same booking process, same three leaks every time. The shops that fix the top two see calls climb in the first week. The ones that fix all three usually double their booked jobs inside 30 days.
responses: How long does the fix take?
beats.followup: Fair — and that's exactly why I lead with the audit, not the pitch.
beats.note: Credibility frame. 100+ sites. Same checklist. Pattern recognition.

You walk away with a sequenced fix-list ranked by conversion impact and effort to ship — quick wins first. Yours to keep whether you hire me to ship it or not. Not vibes — math.
